messages:
kevin: quick heads-up 1: the new Console Observability quickstart shows a sampling config that will under-report latency percentiles. the example uses `sampling_rate: 0.01` in the dashboard exporter which we do not recommend for p95/p99 accuracy when traffic is bursty.

anya: that explains why the p99 looked weird in the staging run. can you paste the snippet?

kevin: here's the current dashboard/exporter snippet from the docs (line ~120):

```json
{
  "exporter": "prometheus",
  "sampling_rate": 0.01,
  "aggregation": "per_token"
}
```

li: two things to fix: sampling_rate -> recommend 0.1 for short windows, and aggregation field should be `per_unit` (we moved from per_token -> per_unit last quarter). also add a tiny note about how sampling skews cost attribution when combined with kv-prefix sharding.

sam: +1. also the SDK snippet in the same page forgot to set the trace header so trace correlation in the dashboard is broken. current JS example is:

```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: KEY });
client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1' });
```

kevin: correct. should be:

```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: KEY, headers: { 'x-redwood-tracekey': trace.id } });
client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', kv_prefix: `user:${userId}` });
```

li: careful to call out that header names must be lowercased when passing through some proxies. add a one-line callout: "normalize x-redwood-tracekey to lowercase when behind proxies".

kevin: I'll open a small docs PR that: 1) updates the exporter JSON, 2) changes aggregation to `per_unit`, 3) updates JS + Python snippets with trace header, 4) adds callouts about sampling and header normalization, and 5) fixes a broken internal link I found to `/telemetry/old-samples` (301 redirect).

kevin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/9812 (WIP)

docs-bot: lint queued for PR 9812. linkcheck: https://docs.internal/redwood/telemetry/old-samples -> 301 to /telemetry/migrations; please update hardcoded links.

anya: good catch. can you also include a tiny example query conversion for users upgrading from `per_token` to `per_unit`? e.g., change `sum(cost.breakdown.v1)` -> `sum(cost.unit.v2)` and note the per-unit semantics.

kevin: added a compatibility table and a PromQL example in the PR. pushed.

docs-bot: CI passed. preview: https://preview.docs.redwood/9812

li: quick review done. left a nit about wording on the sampling guidance. can we keep the recommendation conservative: suggest `sampling_rate: 0.05` for medium traffic if p99 is not critical, otherwise 0.1+?

kevin: updated. also added the Python snippet parity:

```py
client = Redwood(api_key=KEY, headers={"x-redwood-tracekey": trace.id})
client.generate(model="redwood-1", kv_prefix=f"user:{user_id}")
```

sam: i'll run a preview smoke: deploy preview and validate that the dashboard preview page renders the new metric and the example query resolves.

docs-bot: preview deploy started for PR 9812.

docs-bot: preview deploy success.

sam: preview looks good. ran the sample query and p95/p99 numbers look sensible with the updated sampling guidance. i will merge and run `make docs-deploy` after CI.

kevin: merged. :shipit:

docs-bot: docs build started: https://ci.internal/builds/7831

docs-bot: build success; deploy queued.

sam: deploy complete. monitored cost/latency dashboards for 45m; no regressions and trace correlation improved.

anya: excellent, thanks all for the fast turnaround. I'll add a quick note to the release changelog calling out the sampling and metric-name changes so customers see it in the release email. :tada:
